name: consume-input-peak-memory

protocol.note: Both variants perform the identical real transform (a linear RGBA8Unorm buffer allocation transformed into a real MTLTexture SampleFacet via TASK-C2's ensure_texture, then Arena::transform() to advance representation_epoch). multi-version-baseline mirrors the traditional explicit-fence-and-manual-reuse scheme: it deliberately never calls Arena::consume(), so the old linear backing stays resident alongside the new texture indefinitely. consume-input additionally calls Arena::consume() once the new representation is live, honoring ConsumeInput's real contract (Arena::consume requires an epoch-matched lookup and in_flight==0, then retires the allocation) -- the old backing's host bytes are then actually freed (not merely reported as freed), and completion_delay_ns measures the real host wall-clock time from the epoch bump to that retirement completing.

correctness.oracle: arithmetic: peak_bytes == old_backing_bytes + new_backing_bytes for both variants (same workload, so this must match exactly); steady_bytes == peak_bytes for multi-version-baseline (nothing retired); steady_bytes == new_backing_bytes for consume-input (old backing actually retired)
correctness.tolerance: exact (integer byte counts, no floating-point involved)

fault_injection.reason: The catalog names 'fault before/during/after transform; capture replay request; external reference exists' as required fault-injection variants. This codebase's existing fault/poison mechanism (core::PoisonState/FaultRecord/ExecutionResult, ADR-005/ADR-009) is scoped to ir::Module instruction execution (instruction_index, ir::Effect, task_index) inside compile()/submit() -- run_consume_input performs no IR module execution at all (it is a standalone Arena+Metal-texture operation, the same standalone shape as run_cull_compact/run_sample_facet). Reusing that mechanism here is not possible without inventing a new, unrelated fault-injection concept for Arena-level transform/consume calls specifically. Rather than fabricate fault-injection results to fill this metric, this milestone reports it honestly as Deferred; a future milestone that needs it would need to design that mechanism for real, scoped to Arena::transform/consume, not adapt the IR-execution fault path.

judgement: consume-input demonstrates a real, measured steady-state memory reduction relative to the multi-version-baseline for an identical linear-to-sample-optimal transform (verified on real Apple Silicon hardware: peak 32 bytes, baseline steady 32 bytes, consume-input steady 16 bytes -- a 50% reduction for this fixture's 2x2 RGBA8Unorm workload). Per the catalog's judgement rule ('ConsumeInput is enabled only when the proof succeeds; the reduced watermark and lost replay/rollback capability must be explicitly quantified'): the watermark reduction is the steady_bytes delta above; what is explicitly given up is that consume-input's old linear backing is unrecoverable after Arena::consume() retires it (its bytes are cleared, its allocation id can never satisfy a future epoch-matched lookup at the old generation) -- there is no replay/rollback to the pre-transform representation once ConsumeInput has run, whereas multi-version-baseline retains the old backing precisely so such a rollback stays possible. Fault-injection coverage is explicitly Deferred (see fault_injection above), not silently omitted.
vulkan_status: compile-review-only (ADR-024/030); no Vulkan-side ConsumeInput wiring was attempted in this milestone (no Vulkan hardware reachable on this host, and this milestone's transform target -- SampleFacet -- is itself compile-review-only on Vulkan per E008)
